scope: Same finite pin, nut pocket and V faces in actual carrier-local coordinates. Nominal rigid CAD and maintained contact branch. Not an actual threaded-fit/metrology/preload certificate or full C/H/K/P elimination.

new_actual_constraint.meaning: At the same installed nut mid-plane, its guaranteed R2.75 outer circle must fit the real AF5.8 hex pocket. The pin axis is the same coaxial threaded-axis line in the nominal fastener model. Nut rotation around its own axis is not set to zero.

joint_variables.q_i: n_i dot w, n1=(1,-1)/sqrt2,n2=(1,1)/sqrt2; orthonormal pair
joint_variables.delta0: same pin centre minus (20,0) at carrier Y3.125
joint_variables.deltaN: same pin centre at installed nut centre Y_N
joint_variables.cam_intersection_identity: C(qcam)=T_i+O_i[20+delta_x(y*), y*, delta_z(y*)]. y* and qcam are the SAME intersection with the real cam section; do not replace y* by10.5 under arbitrary C/K pose.

branch_requirements: Nut axis and shoulder axis are coaxial in the nominal fastener model; real thread play/coaxiality is not supplied.
Follower nut front annulus is seated on its real +Y pocket roof at Y−1.9; shoulder end has at least one contact with its real seat Y1.75. Entire faces need not be assumed fully flush.
Both finite V planes retain at least one actual pin contact; their contacts may occur at different Y and at finite end edges. Full-length generatrix contact is NOT assumed.
From the nominal installed branch, contacts remain retained and rigid solids do not interpenetrate. Nut backing out or V unloading leaves this proof domain.
Current nominal six-sided nut and 32-sided shoulder shapes are used only as outer/inner bounding shapes; no as-purchased tolerances inferred.

finite_contact_backsubstitution.roof_material_test: outer<4mm carrier half-Z; inner>1.7mm M3 passage; M2 cut starts4.8mm from axis, beyond this ring.
finite_contact_backsubstitution.proof: At the upper section limit Y→4.5 from below, inscribed-cylinder support points fall strictly inside the two real diagonal face spans; lower-end cap truncation is allowed. Nut and shoulder finite caps remain covered. Derived slope <.09 prevents a first exit from this finite domain.

inequalities.contact_upper: n_i.delta0 <= h|q_i| + e_i; e_i=Rmax(sqrt(1+q_i²)-1)<=Rmax*q_i²/2. This follows from an actual contact somewhere in the finite Y1.75..4.5 span; no same-Y contact assumption.
inequalities.upper_nonpenetration: n_i.delta0+h q_i >= -rho, rho=2-r_pin_min, from a real inscribed-cylinder point at the finite upper face limit.
inequalities.global_slope: (Dmin-h)||w|| <= cN+sqrt2*rho+(Rmax/2)||w||². On0..guard, monotonic lhs gives its small-root upper bound.
inequalities.positive_q_norm: ||q_plus|| <= smallroot(cN); the negative-q components do not consume an independent second nut-centre budget.
inequalities.negative_q_dropped_from_positive_project: For carrier-local Y10.5, C-h=6 >= Rmax*guard/2=.09. Hence e_i <= (Rmax*guard/2)|q_i| cannot offset the negative linear contribution when q_i<0. Both (1,+/-.625) have nonnegative coefficients in the two V-normal basis directions.
inequalities.common_domain_handling: These are necessary consequences of the SAME nut centre and pin line. Their safe norm outer bounds are not claimed simultaneously attained, and no physical failure is inferred from a loose bound.

radial_projection_bookkeeping.guard: The .372... mixed bound is in carrier-local X/Z at Y10.5 with coefficient(1,±.625). It is NOT automatically the entire finite-pin term in an arbitrarily transformed common cam. Use the exact C/K identity and actual y* before subtracting it from J_common.
radial_projection_bookkeeping.general_y_bound: For y*>=4.5 within the proven full-cylinder interval: ||deltaXZ(y*)|| <= (y*−1.75)wbar +Rmax*wbar²/2+sqrt2*rho. Use this vector set with the same O_i/C, not an independent phase shift.

mechanical_interpretation.current_pin_is_not_geometrically_free: The real captive nut supplies a lower radial registration section; it must not be omitted and then replaced by an invented long V bearing.
mechanical_interpretation.what_does_not_lock_contact: The sliding block ear and compensation stops retain the block, but do not by themselves prove a positive V preload under the cam wrench. The single M2 adjuster acts atY1.5 while pin-contact nose startsY1.95; block moment/pose cannot be replaced by a prescribed zero tilt.
mechanical_interpretation.minimal_next_action: First include this same-nut bound and the finite shoulder slab in the common C/K intersection calculation. This is a tighter nominal constraint, not a reason to change the existing holes merely because an older loose bound failed.
mechanical_interpretation.optional_design_if_retention_or_toleranc: A lockable longer M2 adjuster with an exterior jam nut can retain screw position, after local tool/clearance review; it does not certify preload or remove pin tilt. To remove reliance on a threaded nut as a radial datum, replace the carrier pin location with a positively retained metal round-journal/bushing support over a declared finite span; this requires the corresponding longer journal/seat and real host clearance review, not simply shrinking a PETG hole or calling the existing2.75mm V infinitely long.

numerical_method: Fraction arithmetic, directed1e−12 rounding and conservative square-root bounds. No sampling optimizer; branch guard and finite-domain margins verified analytically.
